findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a d458 acceptance test asserting that a present-local_id ticket with a compacted/empty *-STATUS.json trail degrades to the pre-S6 comment-fallback+drift (no invented hops).
evidence: Parent AC5: '... or when no recorded trail survives, e.g. a compacted ticket ...'
d458 ACs list test_replay_skipped_when_local_id_absent and test_replay_aborts_when_current_status_not_in_sequence, but no test named for a compacted/empty recorded-hop trail with a present local_id.
d458 Context mentions '*-STATUS.json' glob and reducer replay but the plan body does not address snapshot/compaction folding of STATUS events.
findings.finding: Parent AC5 requires that when 'no recorded trail survives — e.g. a compacted ticket whose STATUS events are folded into a snapshot that keeps only the final status — replay is not applicable and the failed transition degrades to the pre-S6 per-mutation soft-fail backstop.' S6 child d458 covers replay-skip when local_id is absent and abort-to-drift on an illegal/absent-from-sequence hop, but does NOT have an acceptance test for the compaction case: a present local_id whose *-STATUS.json events have been compacted away (empty/single-entry recorded_status_hops) degrading to soft-fail. This is the compaction remainder of AC5 named by the parent; d458's recorded_status_hops behavior on an empty glob is implied but not asserted.
scenarios: A ticket whose STATUS events were compacted into a snapshot (final status only) hits an invalid direct transition; replay derives an empty/degenerate hop list and must fall back to soft-fail without inventing hops.
findings.suggested_fix: Add test_replay_degrades_on_compacted_trail (present local_id, recorded_status_hops returns [] or single final) → replay not applicable → comment-fallback + drift, result is None, no transition_issue_by_name calls.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure the priority-drift test module (a881) also resets _DRIFT_WARNED per-test (autouse reset_drift_warnings fixture), mirroring ab9f's status-module fixture.
evidence: ab9f: 'process-global dedupe set _DRIFT_WARNED' reset fixture scoped to 'tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_status_mapping.py'
a881: 'resolve_outbound_priority ... on miss → warn once (reset_drift_warnings sink, :31)' and test_priority_drifts asserts 'a warning is recorded'
ab9f describes the identical pollution class: 'A test that asserts a drift warning IS emitted ... can be polluted under test reordering'
findings.finding: The _DRIFT_WARNED process-global dedupe set is shared by S2 status (438a, resolve_outbound_status) and S5 priority (a881, resolve_outbound_priority), both draining through reset_drift_warnings. ab9f adds an autouse reset fixture ONLY to tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_status_mapping.py. a881's priority drift test (test_priority_drifts, which asserts a warning IS recorded) lives in a separate test file and depends on the same shared global not being pre-populated, but no sibling adds a reset fixture to the priority test module. This is an implicit-shared-state / order-dependence hazard equivalent to the one ab9f was created to fix, left unowned for the priority axis.
scenarios: Under test reordering, a status-mapping test records e.g. a priority value in _DRIFT_WARNED (or vice versa) before a881's test_priority_drifts runs, suppressing the expected priority drift warning and failing the assertion.
findings.suggested_fix: Add an autouse reset_drift_warnings() fixture to a881's priority test file, or move the reset fixture to a shared conftest covering both status and priority mapping test modules.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify S6's replay resume-point rule for a non-injective forward map: which occurrence of the current Jira status name anchors replay when it appears more than once in the recorded hop sequence, and what replay does when the anchor is the final recorded hop (zero remaining hops).
evidence: value_maps.py:78-86 LOCAL_STATUS_TO_JIRA maps {in_progress, blocked} -> 'In Progress' and {closed, cancelled, deleted} -> 'Done' — a repeated Jira name in the forward-mapped hop trail is expected, not exceptional
config.py:52-60 documents that this forward map is non-injective and 'has no inverse'
Plan text says only 'anchors on Jira's current status' with no duplicate-anchor tie-break and no zero-remaining-hop rule — an under-specified load-bearing ordering detail
findings.finding: S6's replay mechanism specifies anchoring on 'Jira's current status' within the forward-mapped recorded hop sequence, but the forward status map is non-injective (blocked & in_progress both map to 'In Progress'; closed/cancelled/deleted all map to 'Done'), so the current Jira status name can appear MORE THAN ONCE in that sequence. The plan does not state which occurrence is chosen as the resume point (nor what happens when the anchor lands on the final recorded hop, i.e. zero remaining hops to replay), leaving replay ordering and termination ambiguous.
findings.location: Approach section ('anchors on Jira's current status, and re-attempts each intermediate hop through that existing single-hop primitive exactly once each, in recorded order'); AC line 'A non-allowed transition is attempted by replay'
scenarios: A ticket that went open -> in_progress -> blocked -> in_progress -> done forward-maps to ['To Do','In Progress','In Progress','In Progress','Done']; when Jira currently shows 'In Progress', which of the three positions is the resume point determines how many hops replay
A ticket currently sitting at the final recorded hop: anchoring there yields zero remaining hops, so replay must not report 'landed' for a ticket that never moved
findings.suggested_fix: State that replay anchors on the LAST occurrence of the current Jira status name (the most-recently-synced state) and aborts to drift when the resume point is the final recorded hop (zero transitions would run), so a stuck ticket is never reported as landed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a brief external prior-art note in the Approach/S6 (and S3) sections comparing the transition-replay-from-STATUS-event-log algorithm and the rebar-type: round-trip collapse label against how established two-way trackers (e.g. Exalate's transition-driven status sync + external status-mapping scripts) handle non-representable transitions and non-injective type mapping, justifying the bespoke design.
evidence: Plan asserts novelty explicitly: 'while S6's replay algorithm itself is new code' and 'S6 adds new dispatcher logic that derives the intended local hop sequence from the ticket's core STATUS event log'.

The plan cites internal ADRs (0083, 0055) and internal primitives (rebar-status: labels, EXCLUDED_SYNC_TYPES) but no external prior art for the replay algorithm or the collapse-label round-trip technique.

Retrieved prior art: Exalate documents transition-based status synchronization and external status-mapping scripts (docs.exalate.com 'Sync Status with External Scripts', Ambientia 'status mapping ... transitions to Awaiting delivery per status mapping') — a directly comparable approach to driving a target's workflow transitions rather than replaying a recorded hop trail.

Retrieved prior art: the layered built-in->default->per-project deep-merge precedence is a standard config pattern (GitLab CI includes 'default' + hash-merge, OpenCode 'project config has highest precedence', Mago 'merged later-wins, deepest-first'), so the seam's config layer is well-trodden and needs no novelty defense — but the two algorithmic pieces do.
findings.finding: The plan flags S6 transition-replay ('S6's replay algorithm itself is new code') and the rebar-type: collapse label as novel/new code but weighs them against no external prior art, even though commercial two-way trackers solve the same non-representable-transition and non-injective-type problems.
findings.location: Approach section (S6 replay paragraph; 'collapse ... made round-trip-safe by a rebar-type: label') and Child decomposition S3/S6
scenarios: Reviewers/implementers cannot tell whether the bespoke event-log replay is justified over an established transition-driven mapping approach (as Exalate uses), risking reinventing a solved integration problem.
The rebar-type: collapse label re-derives a round-trip metadata-preservation technique without checking how existing sync tools round-trip non-injective type mappings.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the f1bc split ordering and the post-split integration line-anchors so 438a/a8ea/a881/2c66 all reference outbound_mutation_builders.py consistently for the same builder functions.
evidence: f1bc: 'Move the pair into a new sibling module outbound_mutation_builders.py. compute_outbound_mutations imports them back.'
a8ea: '_compute_outbound_create_mutation (outbound_mutation_builders.py:37) passes it' and 'Threaded at BOTH outbound_mutation_builders.py sites: create :81/:138; update :276/:281'
438a: 'Compute once at outbound_mutation_builders.py:285'
2c66: 'in _compute_outbound_update_mutation (:163), pass the new local_parents ... into the _diff_comments(...) call (:277)'
findings.finding: f1bc (S-split) MOVES `_compute_outbound_create_mutation` and `_compute_outbound_update_mutation` out of `outbound_differ.py` into a new `outbound_mutation_builders.py`, but sibling children 438a, a8ea, a881, 2c66, and d458 pin concrete line numbers and integration sites in `outbound_differ.py` (e.g. a8ea 'outbound_mutation_builders.py:37/:81/:138/:276/:281' vs 438a 'outbound_mutation_builders.py:285' vs 2c66 'outbound_mutation_builders.py:163/:277' vs d458 'dispatch_one.py:470-472') that assume a specific post-split (or pre-split) file layout. The children reference outbound_mutation_builders.py inconsistently for the SAME functions (e.g. the create mutation builder is at :37 per a8ea but the update path is cited at :163/:277 per 2c66 and :285 per 438a/1515), indicating the line-anchored integration sites were authored against divergent snapshots of the post-f1bc split. Ordering/assumption tension: the exact seam each child edits depends on f1bc landing first and on a shared, stable line map that the children do not agree on.
scenarios: An implementer lands 438a before f1bc split, expecting the builder at outbound_differ.py; or lands after f1bc but finds the line anchors (:285 vs :163 vs :37) do not resolve to the cited function.
findings.suggested_fix: State explicitly that f1bc is a hard prerequisite (it is titled 'prerequisite for S3/S6') and replace brittle line numbers in the dependent children with function-name anchors (e.g. 'in _compute_outbound_create_mutation') so the split does not invalidate them.
